description: Upload a PNG and instantly confirm whether it actually contains transparent pixels, and exactly how much of the image is transparent.

howto: Drop a PNG (or WebP) onto the dropzone.
The tool scans every pixel for an alpha channel below 255.
A clear verdict tells you whether transparency exists and what percentage of the image is transparent.
Use this to confirm your file is truly a transparent PNG before submission or publishing.
Pair it with the Background Edge Checker to inspect the quality of the transparent edges.
features: Image preview on a checkerboard background

faq.a: Any pixel with an alpha value below 255 is considered transparent. Fully transparent pixels have alpha 0 — you can see through them completely.
Some stock platforms reject transparent images unless you have approval, while marketplaces selling cut-outs require it. Knowing for certain avoids surprises at submission time.

faq.q: Does a JPG ever have transparency?
faq.a: No. JPEG has no alpha channel. If a file was saved with .jpg but truly contains transparency, it was actually saved as PNG — run the File Type Detector to confirm the real format.
No. The check runs entirely in your browser by reading the image data locally.
